title: MicroVSA: An Ultra-Lightweight Vector Symbolic Architecture-based Classifier Library for Always-On Inference on Tiny Microcontrollers
problem: Current machine learning algorithms and microcontroller implementations are too expensive and power-consuming for deployment on low-cost, low-power edge devices. Computation requirements of ML models exceed the capabilities of lower-end MCUs.
motivation: Enabling efficient AI inference on tiny edge devices expands deployment possibilities without the cost and power penalties of current solutions.
method: MicroVSA applies Vector Symbolic Architecture (VSA), which represents each pattern as a very-high-dimensional vector—a list with thousands of numbers. To classify new input, it compares the input vector against stored pattern vectors to find the closest match. VSA's key advantage is its approximate computing model: instead of performing exact mathematical operations, it uses fast approximate comparisons that dramatically reduce both the computational work and memory needed to run on tiny microcontrollers.
key_novelty: The core contribution is using Vector Symbolic Architecture to enable classification inference on ultra-tiny, resource-constrained microcontrollers where traditional machine learning is too expensive to run.
contributions: MicroVSA library enabling VSA-based classification on tiny MCUs
Ultra-lightweight inference design suitable for lower-end microcontrollers
Always-on inference capability with minimal power consumption
primary_theme: Ultra-lightweight ML classification for tiny edge devices
